content: Written 2026-10-07 15:22, self-approved. Flat anchor (supervisor 15:20): the official, unmodified GaME (baselines/GaME at its release commit 1c971d6; the only working-tree change is a compile fix, '#include <cstdint>' in flashsplat rasterizer_impl.h) run with its own run.py on GaME_Flat (HF voviktyl/GaME_Flat, local copy datasets/game_flat_hf: run1 400 frames, run2 362, sam_masks.h5 per run). Config = configs/flat/flat.yaml as published with only wandb: False (no external logging) and dataset_path set (runs/game_flat_official_20261007/flat_official.yaml; diff shown in the run log). Output: runs/game_flat_official_20261007/out.

Nothing derived: GaME run.py as released (train run1 then run2's train split; pre_ref eval of run2 train + test; refinement 30000 iterations; post_ref eval; checkpoint). Seed 0 (utils.setup_seed(0) in run.py). Eq. 5 self-check: not applicable (no layer, GaME's own change handling as published).

GaME's own: scale 10 (flat.yaml), depth in metres x 10, test split every 10th frame of run2 except the first (datasets.py get_flat_datasets), metrics of src/utils/mapping_eval.py (PSNR, LPIPS, MS-SSIM, depth L1).
GaME's own evaluate() output (output/local/...), no project readout; the comparison is with the published Flat numbers (GaME paper). Our evaluation tools are not involved in this anchor.
out/ (GaME's evaluation files and checkpoint), run log, run.out with peak GPU memory (nvidia-smi sampled every 30 s into vram.log).
The same GaME code path runs inside update_layer every day (TrackedGaME wraps it); the dataset loader is GaME's own FlatDataset; a failure in loading shows in the first minute (watched).

GPU idle (446 MiB used) and the TSDF runner not active; flock runs/GPU.lock. num_label_channels 256 as published: peak unknown on 16 GB (published on A100); an OOM is reported as infeasible with the published config, no change made. Disk: vhdx 449.7 GB, used inside 359 GB, D: free 357 GB; output a few GB.

Expected: runs to the end in about 45-75 min (about 360 keyframes x 50-200 iterations + 30000 refinement iterations); test PSNR near the published Flat value; refuted if it OOMs (then: infeasible as published) or if test PSNR is far (> 2 dB) from the published value (then: check the data copy before anything else).
